issues.description: The problem statement's UML and task text declare numberOfTutors as type int, but the solution implementation declares the field and some related signatures using short (field and constructor/setter parameter). This creates a type inconsistency: students guided by the UML will expect int for numberOfTutors when implementing getters, setters and the constructor, while the solution uses short. This may confuse students about the correct type to use and can cause signature mismatches (e.g., setNumberOfTutors(short) vs. an expected setNumberOfTutors(int)).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of numberOfTutors consistent with the problem statement UML. Change the field, constructor parameter and setter parameter to int (and keep the getter returning int), or alternatively update the UML and task text to specify short if that was intended. Prefer using int for numberOfTutors for consistency with the UML and other numeric attributes.
